threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can find a parking spot on Lower Clapton Road after 6 PM without circling for ages. Welcome to reality!
Heard a group of lads on the 35 last night arguing about which chicken shop is the best in Brixton. Hilarious how passionate they got about it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The morning smell of fresh bagels from the corner shop mixed with the sound of a street performer playing on a broken guitar—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip coffee while dodging a spontaneous art installation made from old subway signs. It's part of the charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to carry a light jacket year-round—those fogs roll in unexpectedly, but tourists think it's always sunny. Classic S.F.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy using a broom as a makeshift microphone on the 49. He was belting out 'Don't Stop Believin''—Muni gold. The whole bus was singing along.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar in Gràcia serves tapas, but many still stick to vermut and olives. It's a whole vibe, not just food.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look confused by the menu at the local tapas bar, especially when they ask for ketchup with their patatas bravas.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Blackstock Road bus is the fastest way to get to Finsbury Park. Everyone else just bikes it or walks through the park.
Caught a guy on the 333 last night singing opera to himself. Did a whole aria before the driver told him to pipe down. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a random guy painting a mural on the bus stop while the bus was late, and everyone just sat there, sipping their coffee like it was normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that doubles as a dance studio on weekends; grab a beer and watch the tango lessons unfold!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local rolls their eyes when someone asks for directions to the 'BART station'—it's always 'Civic Center' or 'Powell,' never just 'the BART.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus trying to barter a sandwich for a single fare. The driver just shook his head, but the whole bus cracked up.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume all bars close by 2am, but in Gràcia, the real life starts after midnight—it's when the locals come out to play.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by their hesitation at the metro turnstiles—always looking for the right way to swipe their T-10.
